A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a systematic way of constructing quasi-cyclic LDPCS with good error performance for the two channels mentioned above, and the codes are based on finite field arithmetic.

we construct quasi-cyclic LDPCS for AWGN and binary erasure channels with a very simple parity check matrix, which is the identity matrix, and the parity check matrix can be easily constructed from a generator matrix.

the quasi-cyclic LDPCS constructed here are based on the following: (i) finite fields, (ii) special representations of finite field vectors, (iii) special vector representations of matrix elements, (iv) the cyclic property, and (v) a special structure of the parity-check matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the algebraic structure of the code allows us to derive an exact expression for the bit and symbol error probabilities, and to obtain the threshold SNR for errorless transmission.

, by using a vector representation of finite field elements, we can construct a class of quasi cyclic LDPC codes for which the number of parity checks is a small constant multiple of the number of information bits.
